from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Stretch' Concept", [
            "Linear transformations deform space like stretching rubber.",
            "Most vectors rotate during the deformation process.",
            "Eigenvectors are special directions remaining fixed."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        rubber_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rubber.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(grid, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(rubber_icon, "A5", scale_factor=0.2)
        space_label = Text("Space", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(space_label, "B5")
        self.play(Create(grid), FadeIn(rubber_icon), Write(space_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        deformation_label = Text("Deformation", color="#00BFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(deformation_label, "E5")
        
        # Apply transformation to grid
        self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix([[1.5, 0.5], [0, 1.2]]), Write(deformation_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        eigen_vec = Vector([1, 0], color="#FFA500")
        self.place_at_grid(eigen_vec, "C3")
        
        self.play(Create(eigen_vec), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Definition: The Eigen-Equation", [
            "Eigen-equation is Av equals lambda times v.",
            "Lambda represents the scaling factor of elongation.",
            "Det A minus lambda I equals zero."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the matrix equation A * v = λ * v in white
        equation = MathTex("A", "v", "=", "\\lambda", "v")
        equation[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # A yellow
        equation[1].set_color("#00FF00") # v green
        equation[4].set_color("#00FF00") # v green
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Lambda represents the scaling factor
        self.play(Indicate(equation[3]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Det A minus lambda I equals zero
        det_eq = MathTex("\\text{det}(A - \\lambda I) = 0")
        self.place_at_grid(det_eq, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(det_eq))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Eigenbasis", [
            "Eigenvectors can form a coordinate basis.",
            "The matrix becomes diagonal in this basis.",
            "Complex calculations simplify to independent scaling."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg]
        grid_bg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        
        plane = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([-1, 1], color=WHITE)
        
        group = VGroup(grid_bg, plane, v1, v2)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'C2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_bg), Create(plane), GrowArrow(v1), GrowArrow(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform to show diagonal/scaling
        self.play(
            plane.animate.stretch(1.5, 0).stretch(0.5, 1),
            v1.animate.set_length(2).set_color(BLUE),
            v2.animate.set_length(1).set_color(BLUE)
        )
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Use ruler to measure
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, 'B3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(ruler))
        v1_highlight = v1.copy().set_color("#32CD32")
        v2_highlight = v2.copy().set_color("#32CD32")
        self.play(FadeIn(v1_highlight), FadeIn(v2_highlight))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Vibration & Stability", [
            "Eigenvalues represent system vibration frequencies.",
            "Eigenvectors define the bridge's vibration shape.",
            "Resonance occurs at specific eigen-frequencies."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # Load assets
        bridge = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg")
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # Light yellow
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Overlay eigen-mode vectors at resonance in magenta (#FF00FF)
        self.place_in_area(bridge, 'C1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.6)
        eigen_vector.next_to(bridge, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge), GrowArrow(eigen_vector))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#0000FF") # Light blue
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'Stable/Unstable' label as eigenvalues change in red (#FF4500).
        label = Text("Unstable", color="#FF4500", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00") # Light green
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Stretch' Concept
sections.content: Introduce linear transformation as a visual deformation of space. Explain that while most vectors change direction when a matrix is applied, 'Eigenvectors' are the special directions that stay fixed on their original span.
sections.example: Visualize a grid of rubber bands: Applying a matrix is like stretching the grid. Most arrows rotate, but an eigenvector remains pointing along the same line, just elongated or compressed.

sections.title: Mathematical Definition: The Eigen-Equation
sections.content: Define Av = λv. Explain that 'v' (eigenvector) is the direction, and 'λ' (eigenvalue) is the scaling factor. Emphasize that for a non-zero vector to exist, det(A - λI) must equal zero.
sections.example: If matrix A scales a vector v by 3, λ=3. The equation Av = 3v shows the output is just a scalar multiple of the input.

sections.title: Visualizing Eigenbasis
sections.content: Explain that if we have enough linearly independent eigenvectors, they form a 'basis' for the space. In this basis, the transformation matrix becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making complex calculations trivial.
sections.example: Imagine a 2D plane defined by two eigenvectors. Instead of using x and y coordinates, we describe the world using 'eigen-coordinates', where every movement is just an independent stretch along these two axes.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Vibration & Stability
sections.content: Connect the concept to physical systems. Eigenvalues represent natural frequencies of vibration, and eigenvectors represent the 'shape' of those vibrations.
sections.example: A suspension bridge: Eigenvectors represent the specific shapes the bridge can bend into, and eigenvalues represent the frequencies at which it might collapse due to resonance.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Recap: Eigenvectors = Directions that don't rotate; Eigenvalues = Scale factors; Eigenbasis = A simplified coordinate system.
sections.example: A quick visual quiz: Show a transformation animation and ask students to identify the direction that did not rotate (the eigenvector).
